evidence.claim: The report lists credible reports of unlawful and arbitrary killings, forced disappearances, torture by government, arbitrary arrest, serious restrictions on expression and media, and weak accountability for major abuses.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: The report lists credible reports of unlawful and arbitrary killings, forced disappearances, torture by government, arbitrary arrest, serious restrictions on expression and media, and weak accountability for major abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official US government human-rights report summarizing the year's record.
evidence.period_fit: Covers events of 2022 and the year-end rights picture
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level record under Buhari's administration; not proof of his personal order, but directly relevant to ruler responsibility.
contrary_evidence: The summary is broad and does not isolate Buhari's direct command in each case.
It aggregates multiple issue areas rather than a single incident.

evidence.claim: Security services reportedly committed torture and inhuman treatment of suspects, detainees, and prisoners, and Amnesty documented 62 cases of arbitrary arrest, ill-treatment, and torture in southeastern states.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: Security services reportedly committed torture and inhuman treatment of suspects, detainees, and prisoners, and Amnesty documented 62 cases of arbitrary arrest, ill-treatment, and torture in southeastern states.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Directly quoted government report with a cited NGO corroboration inside it.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target-year conduct and immediate reporting window
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not uniquely Buhari-personal, but squarely within the federal security apparatus he headed.
contrary_evidence: The cited Amnesty material is location-specific rather than nationwide.
The report does not show which abuses had direct presidential awareness.

evidence.claim: HRW cites a UN report saying Boko Haram affiliates abducted and recruited children, including girls, and notes that over 45 children alleged to be associated with armed groups were detained by the military; Nigeria also signed a UN handover protocol in September 2022.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: HRW cites a UN report saying Boko Haram affiliates abducted and recruited children, including girls, and notes that over 45 children alleged to be associated with armed groups were detained by the military; Nigeria also signed a UN handover protocol in September 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent synthesis with a specific 2022 protective measure and a child-detention problem.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The abuses are mostly inherited/non-state or military-conflict context; the handover protocol is a state remedial action under Buhari's government.
contrary_evidence: The underlying child-abduction data are from 2021, so this is partly inherited baseline rather than new 2022 conduct.
The handover protocol is protective but limited in scope.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the vast majority of arrested #EndSARS protesters were still arbitrarily detained without trial, and that inquiry panels had failed to deliver justice for police brutality victims.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Two years on, more than 40 #EndSARS protesters still languishing in jail
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the vast majority of arrested #EndSARS protesters were still arbitrarily detained without trial, and that inquiry panels had failed to deliver justice for police brutality victims.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights investigation with named detainee examples and accountability criticism.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 detention and accountability state
evidence.ruler_attribution: Federal-state police and justice system under Buhari's administration; not evidence of a single presidential order but of tolerated impunity.
contrary_evidence: A few detainees were released in 2022, so the record is not total stasis.
This concerns the afterlife of 2020 protests, not a fresh 2022 crackdown.

evidence.claim: Buhari said lethal military force was considered for the Kaduna train hostages but was reluctantly discarded because collateral damage could not be assured, and he said his primary concern was to get everyone released safe and unhurt.
evidence.title: President Buhari Assures that Government will do Its Best to Secure Release of Remaining Abductees
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said lethal military force was considered for the Kaduna train hostages but was reluctantly discarded because collateral damage could not be assured, and he said his primary concern was to get everyone released safe and unhurt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential explanation of a domestic security choice with explicit restraint reasoning.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari and strongly relevant to restraint under pressure.
contrary_evidence: The need to choose among bad options reflects a severe security failure.
The hostages remained captive for months, so restraint did not equal immediate success.

evidence.claim: Buhari condemned attacks on non-indigenes and law enforcement officials in the southeast, promised a speedy investigation, and said the killings were sad and unwelcome.
evidence.title: President Buhari Calls South East Killings Sad And Unwelcome
evidence.excerpt: Buhari condemned attacks on non-indigenes and law enforcement officials in the southeast, promised a speedy investigation, and said the killings were sad and unwelcome.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement on a dated State House page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari as president.
contrary_evidence: Condemnation is not the same as prevention or successful prosecution.
The statement does not show whether investigators achieved results.

evidence.claim: Buhari urged Nigerians to settle grievances peacefully, called on aspirants to avoid hate speech and divisive tendencies, and said violence generally mars elections.
evidence.title: Independence Day Address By President Buhari On Nigeria's 62nd Independence Anniversary Celebration
evidence.excerpt: Buhari urged Nigerians to settle grievances peacefully, called on aspirants to avoid hate speech and divisive tendencies, and said violence generally mars elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit anti-incitement and anti-violence language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari, though it is rhetoric rather than an operational security order.
contrary_evidence: Rhetoric alone does not show actual protection outcomes.
The address is self-presenting and may overstate government success.

evidence.claim: Buhari directed the armed forces to remain apolitical, improve human-rights obligations, and support a peaceful environment for the 2023 general elections.
evidence.title: President Buhari Canvasses Army Neutrality On 2023 Polls, Wants Human Rights Obligations Sustained
evidence.excerpt: Buhari directed the armed forces to remain apolitical, improve human-rights obligations, and support a peaceful environment for the 2023 general elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instruction on a dated State House page.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 ruler conduct with direct domestic-safety relevance
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari as commander-in-chief and relevant to civilian protection.
contrary_evidence: This is forward-looking guidance, not a proven outcome.
The speech is aimed at elections rather than everyday policing.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Sokoto declared a 24-hour curfew after protests over Deborah Samuel's killing, with police firing tear gas and live bullets in the air; Buhari condemned the killing and called for an impartial investigation.
evidence.title: Nigeria's Sokoto state declares curfew over student killing protests
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Sokoto declared a 24-hour curfew after protests over Deborah Samuel's killing, with police firing tear gas and live bullets in the air; Buhari condemned the killing and called for an impartial investigation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated contemporaneous event report with clear incident description and presidential reaction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The incident was local, but Buhari's condemnation is directly attributable and the state response reflects the domestic safety climate.
contrary_evidence: The curfew response shows state containment, not solved underlying tensions.
The article is a short event report rather than a deep accountability investigation.

evidence.claim: SERAP went to court to force publication of the Twitter agreement because it feared the terms could jeopardize freedom of expression, and the government had suspended Twitter after Buhari's tweet was deleted.
evidence.title: Rights group goes to court to get Nigeria to publish agreement with Twitter
evidence.excerpt: SERAP went to court to force publication of the Twitter agreement because it feared the terms could jeopardize freedom of expression, and the government had suspended Twitter after Buhari's tweet was deleted.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on contemporaneous legal challenge and government position, with specific references to Buhari's tweet and the suspension.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Buhari's administration and information ministry, though not necessarily to Buhari's personal day-to-day direction.
contrary_evidence: Twitter had been restored by the time of the report, so the ban was not continuously in force in 2022.
This is a legal dispute over speech controls, not a physical-violence incident.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Buhari decision on nuclear brinkmanship, command-and-control, or other existential-risk use of presidential authority.
No independent audit of whether the 2021-2022 safeguards and physical-protection framework was actually implemented in practice.
No direct evidence of Buhari personally directing external military operations, proxy conduct, or coercive cross-border action in 2022.
No substantive mediation track or concrete ceasefire result led by Buhari himself.
Independent, case-level follow-through on prosecutions and investigations for major 2022 abuses is thin.
Some severe insecurity items are still better understood as state failure in a violent environment than as direct ruler-directed violence.
No independent pre-election audit of how fully the Electoral Act 2022 was implemented before the 2023 polls.
Much of the affirmative evidence is self-description from Buhari and his administration.
Budget execution and capital-spending delivery are not independently audited at the project level here.
Household-level and regional distributional causality remains only partially evidenced.
Independent audit evidence on how much of the announced welfare and health delivery actually reached beneficiaries in 2022 is limited.
The chapter still mixes federal action, donor support, and inherited deprivation.
No direct 2022 evidence of Buhari's assets, procurement benefits, bribes, or formal audit/court findings tied to personal enrichment.
The family-appointment case is strong on patronage but still thin on Buhari's knowledge, benefit, and intent beyond approval.
The Lake Chad arms claim is shown as unsupported, but there is no public correction or retraction by Buhari in the package.
Independent audit-grade evidence on the delivery tracker and the administration's correction of weak implementers is still limited.
The chapter still depends heavily on macro outcomes that mix Buhari-era policy with inherited constraints and external shocks.
